subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A wave-cut notch is formed at the:
options: Base of a cliff where waves erode a hollow
questions.explain: Waves erode a hollow at the cliff base called a wave-cut notch, undercutting the cliff above.

questions.q: Which is a HUMAN cause of increased river flooding?
options: Building on floodplains and creating impermeable surfaces
questions.explain: Urbanisation adds impermeable surfaces and drains, speeding water into rivers.

questions.q: On a coast with alternating hard and soft rock, resistant rock tends to form ____ and softer rock forms ____.
questions.explain: Resistant rock juts out as headlands while softer rock is eroded back into bays.

questions.q: When rocks knock together and become smaller and rounder, the process is:
questions.explain: Attrition wears rocks down as they collide, making them smaller and rounder.

questions.q: On the INSIDE of a meander bend, where the water is slower, the river usually:
options: Deposits sediment forming a slip-off slope (point bar)
questions.explain: Slower flow on the inner bend deposits sediment, building a gently sloping point bar.

questions.q: Erosion caused by the sheer force of fast-moving water hitting and pushing into cracks in the bank is called:
questions.explain: Hydraulic action is the force of water compressing air in cracks, weakening rock.

questions.q: Which sequence shows the correct order in which erosional landforms develop on a headland?
questions.explain: A crack becomes a cave, then an arch, then a stack when the arch collapses, then a stump.

questions.q: On the outside of a meander bend, the river mainly:
options: Erodes, forming a steep river cliff
Deposits sediment forming a slip-off slope
questions.explain: Faster flow on the outer bend erodes the bank, creating a river cliff.

questions.q: In the water cycle, water soaking down into the soil is called:
questions.explain: Infiltration is the movement of water from the surface down into the soil.

questions.q: The water that flows over the surface into a river without soaking in is called:
questions.explain: Surface run-off (overland flow) is water moving across the ground straight into the river.

questions.q: Managed retreat (coastal realignment) involves:
options: Allowing low-value land to flood and the coastline to move back
questions.explain: Managed retreat lets the sea flood low-value land, creating natural defences like salt marsh.

questions.q: Which of these is HARD engineering coastal defence?
questions.explain: A sea wall is a hard engineering structure that reflects wave energy.

questions.q: Transport in which small particles bounce along the river bed is called:
questions.explain: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping of small particles along the bed.

questions.q: Which is an example of HARD engineering river flood management?
options: Building a concrete dam and reservoir
Allowing the river to flood washland
questions.explain: Dams and reservoirs are hard engineering structures that control river flow.

questions.q: The breaking down of rock in place (without movement) by weather, plants or chemicals is called:
questions.explain: Weathering breaks rock down in situ, unlike erosion which also wears away and removes it.

questions.q: The process by which water turns from liquid into vapour and rises into the atmosphere is:
questions.explain: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapour that rises into the air.

questions.q: A waterfall and its plunge pool are typically formed where the river crosses:
options: A band of soft rock over hard rock
A band of hard rock over softer rock
questions.explain: Soft rock beneath a hard cap is eroded faster, forming a waterfall and plunge pool.

questions.q: The change in direction at the end of a spit, forming a curved hook, is mainly caused by:
options: A change in the coastline shape or a second wind/wave direction
questions.explain: A secondary wind or wave direction, or a bend in the coast, curves the end of a spit into a recurved hook.

questions.q: Freeze-thaw weathering on a cliff happens when:
options: Water in cracks freezes, expands and widens the rock until pieces break off
questions.explain: Repeated freezing and expanding of water in cracks widens them until fragments shatter off.

questions.q: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries is the:
questions.explain: A drainage basin is the whole area of land drained by a river system.

questions.q: A wave-cut platform is formed as:
options: A cliff retreats, leaving a rocky surface at its base
A stack collapses into a stump
Sediment is deposited at a river mouth
questions.explain: As waves undercut and the cliff retreats, a flat rocky platform is left at the base.

questions.q: Constructive waves are best described as:
options: Waves that flow inland as rivers
Low, gentle waves with a strong swash that build up beaches
High, frequent waves with a strong backwash that erode beaches
Waves that only occur in storms
questions.explain: Constructive waves have a strong swash and weak backwash, depositing material to build beaches.
